decks.module: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Continually search ahead, beside and behind the.
cards.back: Continually search ahead, beside and behind the vehicle, keeping the eyes moving rather than staring.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Early hazard detection creates time.
cards.back: Early hazard detection creates time to change speed or direction.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: The driver must have a clear.
cards.back: The driver must have a clear view through all windows, windshield and mirrors.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Keep the windshield clean, stop to clean it.
cards.back: Keep the windshield clean, stop to clean it when necessary and maintain a full washer reservoir.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Smoking creates a film inside the windows, so.
cards.back: Smoking creates a film inside the windows, so clean the interior glass frequently if you smoke.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Before driving, remove snow, frost and ice.
cards.back: Before driving, remove snow, frost and ice from every window and from headlamps and taillamps.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not hang mirror objects or place.
cards.back: Do not hang mirror objects or place windshield decals where they block the driver’s view.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: If the license requires corrective.
cards.back: If the license requires corrective lenses, wear them whenever driving.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Keep spare glasses in the vehicle in.
cards.back: Keep spare glasses in the vehicle in case the regular pair is lost or damaged.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Look well ahead to plan the path, leaving.
cards.back: Look well ahead to plan the path, leaving space behind large vehicles that would block the view.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: The manual recommends scanning twenty to thirty seconds ahead.
cards.back: The manual recommends scanning twenty to thirty seconds ahead, taking in the whole scene rather than only the road center.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Include roadside people, vehicles, warning and direction.
cards.back: Include roadside people, vehicles, warning and direction signs, and animals in the forward search.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: If you see a deer, use the.
cards.back: If you see a deer, use the horn and look for others following it.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: A person entering a parked car can warn that.
cards.back: A person entering a parked car can warn that a door may reopen or the car may move into the lane.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Look especially to the sides near busy shopping.
cards.back: Look especially to the sides near busy shopping or parking areas, construction, sidewalks, schools, parks and sales.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: The illustrated school-crossing warning has a.
cards.back: The illustrated school-crossing warning has a five-sided pedestrian symbol above a directional arrow.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: The signed school-zone guidance sets fifteen miles per hour.
cards.back: The signed school-zone guidance sets fifteen miles per hour during recess, when children arrive or leave during opening or closing hours, or when school-speed lights flash during those hours.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Approach tracks looking both ways and anticipate vehicles.
cards.back: Approach tracks looking both ways and anticipate vehicles such as buses and tank trucks that must stop.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: In heavy traffic, wait before the.
cards.back: In heavy traffic, wait before the railroad tracks rather than stopping on them.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Slow and check both directions at a railroad crossing.
cards.back: Slow and check both directions at a railroad crossing even if its warning light is not flashing, since the equipment may not be working.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Flashing railroad red lights require a stop.
cards.back: Flashing railroad red lights require a stop at least fifteen feet from the crossing.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Never drive around a.
cards.back: Never drive around a railroad gate or barrier.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: At multiple tracks, wait after a train passes until.
cards.back: At multiple tracks, wait after a train passes until both directions are visible because another train may approach.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not shift a manual.
cards.back: Do not shift a manual transmission while crossing railroad tracks.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: An Exempt track sign does not guarantee that.
cards.back: An Exempt track sign does not guarantee that the track is unused; check for trains there too.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Check the rear mirror every six to eight.
cards.back: Check the rear mirror every six to eight seconds to track following traffic and rear space.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Check behind when changing lanes, slowing.
cards.back: Check behind when changing lanes, slowing, stopping or before entering an intersection.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Check behind before backing or descending a long or.
cards.back: Check behind before backing or descending a long or steep hill, and look briefly in the mirrors before a sudden slowdown.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Before slowing for a hidden hazard, a side-road turn.
cards.back: Before slowing for a hidden hazard, a side-road turn, parking or pedestrians, check whether following traffic can react.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Allow extra space around drivers whose views are blocked.
cards.back: Allow extra space around drivers whose views are blocked, who are reversing or whose windows are obscured by snow or ice.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Give extra space to potentially distracted delivery or.
cards.back: Give extra space to potentially distracted delivery or construction workers and children who may enter the road.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Expect sudden moves from confused tourists.
cards.back: Expect sudden moves from confused tourists or drivers slowing without an obvious reason.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: If a driver overtakes toward a curve or oncoming.
cards.back: If a driver overtakes toward a curve or oncoming traffic, slow and allow the vehicle back into your lane.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: If another driver may be forced into your lane.
cards.back: If another driver may be forced into your lane by an obstruction or road user, slow and move right as far as practical.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Safe speed depends on road and traffic conditions.
cards.back: Safe speed depends on road and traffic conditions, the speed limit and a safe following distance.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: On a long or steep uphill approach, check.
cards.back: On a long or steep uphill approach, check mirrors early for trucks or buses building speed.
cards.memory_hook: Seeing and responding to road controls

cards.front: Complete the rule: Slow before a curve and choose a.
cards.back: Slow before a curve and choose a speed that permits slight acceleration through it.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Slow further in a curve when grip is poor.
cards.back: Slow further in a curve when grip is poor, another vehicle is ahead or the curve’s end is not visible.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Hard braking in a curve, excessive speed or a.
cards.back: Hard braking in a curve, excessive speed or a very sharp curve can cause loss of tire grip and a skid.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The illustrated angular left arrow warns of a sharp.
cards.back: The illustrated angular left arrow warns of a sharp left curve, while the curved right arrow warns of a right curve.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Reduce speed at the first signs of rain, snow.
cards.back: Reduce speed at the first signs of rain, snow, sleet or ice because slippery roads increase stopping and steering difficulty.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The manual’s wet-road guideline is a speed.
cards.back: The manual’s wet-road guideline is a speed reduction of five to ten miles per hour.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For packed snow, the guidance is to reduce to.
cards.back: For packed snow, the guidance is to reduce to half the dry-road speed; on ice, slow to a crawl.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Wet leaves, gravel and falling or.
cards.back: Wet leaves, gravel and falling or drifting snow can make a road slippery.

cards.front: Complete the rule: At the start of rain, road oil can.
cards.back: At the start of rain, road oil can create particularly slippery pavement until it washes away.

cards.front: Complete the rule: On cold wet days, bridges and overpasses.
cards.back: On cold wet days, bridges and overpasses tend to freeze first and dry last.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Road ice near freezing can be wetter.
cards.back: Road ice near freezing can be wetter and more slippery than at colder temperatures.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a.
cards.back: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a water film rather than maintaining road contact.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Heavy rain and high speed can eliminate tire.
cards.back: Heavy rain and high speed can eliminate tire contact, with worn tires doing so at lower speeds.

cards.front: Complete the rule: To reduce hydroplaning risk, keep tires in.
cards.back: To reduce hydroplaning risk, keep tires in good condition and slow on wet roads.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not drive into a large body of standing.
cards.back: Do not drive into a large body of standing water; use another route if the road is flooded.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Total stopping distance extends from recognizing the need.
cards.back: Total stopping distance extends from recognizing the need to stop until the vehicle is fully stopped.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Higher speed increases the time.
cards.back: Higher speed increases the time and distance needed to stop.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Perception time is the interval needed to recognize that.
cards.back: Perception time is the interval needed to recognize that stopping is necessary; the manual gives an alert-driver average of three-quarters to one second.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Reaction time covers moving from accelerator to brake and.
cards.back: Reaction time covers moving from accelerator to brake and starting braking; the manual gives an average of three-quarters to one second.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Braking distance is the vehicle’s.
cards.back: Braking distance is the vehicle’s stopping travel once braking occurs.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A posted speed is a maximum rather than a.
cards.back: A posted speed is a maximum rather than a required driving speed; slow further when road or weather conditions make it unsafe.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Unless a sign states otherwise, the listed Maine maximum.
cards.back: Unless a sign states otherwise, the listed Maine maximum outside business, residential or built-up areas is forty-five miles per hour.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Unless posted otherwise, the listed maximum in a business.
cards.back: Unless posted otherwise, the listed maximum in a business, residential or built-up district is twenty-five miles per hour.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Exceeding a posted school-zone limit.
cards.back: Exceeding a posted school-zone limit brings twice the usual speeding fine.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Exceeding a posted speed limit, highway.
cards.back: Exceeding a posted speed limit, highway racing and reckless driving are prohibited.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not obstruct normal reasonable traffic by driving too.
cards.back: Do not obstruct normal reasonable traffic by driving too slowly unless a lower speed is needed for safety.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Some highways.
cards.back: Some highways post minimum speeds.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Tire and road condition determine available grip.
cards.back: Tire and road condition determine available grip, so replace tires before the tread becomes unsafe.

cards.front: Complete the rule: At night, keep speed low enough to stop.
cards.back: At night, keep speed low enough to stop within the illuminated distance you can actually see.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If heavy rain, snow or dense fog prevents adequate.
cards.back: If heavy rain, snow or dense fog prevents adequate vision even at low speed, leave the road and wait for improvement.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Approach a blind intersection slowly enough to stop.
cards.back: Approach a blind intersection slowly enough to stop for a vehicle emerging from behind an obstruction.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Slow before a steep hill or sharp curve.
cards.back: Slow before a steep hill or sharp curve so you can stop for a hazard beyond it.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Allow space beside parked vehicles and be ready.
cards.back: Allow space beside parked vehicles and be ready to stop for doors or people emerging between them.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Heavy traffic reduces available space and.
cards.back: Heavy traffic reduces available space and reaction room, requiring a lower speed.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Reduce speed in busy shopping or downtown areas, narrow.
cards.back: Reduce speed in busy shopping or downtown areas, narrow bridges or tunnels, toll plazas and places with schools or playgrounds.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Repeatedly passing slower traffic increases opportunities for conflict.
cards.back: Repeatedly passing slower traffic increases opportunities for conflict even when your own speed remains within the limit.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If many cars are trying to pass, permit safe.
cards.back: If many cars are trying to pass, permit safe passing by easing speed or pulling right rather than forcing traffic to bunch behind.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For freeway entry, find a gap and accelerate in.
cards.back: For freeway entry, find a gap and accelerate in the entrance lane to merge smoothly at highway traffic speed.

cards.front: Complete the rule: On an expressway exit, do not.
cards.back: On an expressway exit, do not decelerate until reaching the exit lane.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Adjust speed early when approaching a slow-moving vehicle, especially.
cards.back: Adjust speed early when approaching a slow-moving vehicle, especially one losing speed uphill or taking longer to accelerate.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A red-bordered orange triangle identifies the slow-moving vehicles described.
cards.back: A red-bordered orange triangle identifies the slow-moving vehicles described, which usually travel at twenty-five miles per hour or less.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Warning signs call for reducing speed to.
cards.back: Warning signs call for reducing speed to allow time to react to the hazard ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The pictured traffic-light warning is a.
cards.back: The pictured traffic-light warning is a yellow diamond containing the red-yellow-green signal image.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The pictured merging warning shows a.
cards.back: The pictured merging warning shows a right branch joining the through lane ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Opposing vertical arrows on a.
cards.back: Opposing vertical arrows on a yellow diamond warn of two-way traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The divided-highway-ends picture warns that.
cards.back: The divided-highway-ends picture warns that the central separation ends ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The divided-highway-begins picture warns of.
cards.back: The divided-highway-begins picture warns of a central separation starting ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A deer silhouette on a yellow.
cards.back: A deer silhouette on a yellow diamond warns of a deer-crossing area.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The illustrated right-lane-end warning.
cards.back: The illustrated right-lane-end warning directs traffic to merge left.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The bicycle warning calls for extra.
cards.back: The bicycle warning calls for extra attention to bicycles or a bicycle crossing.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The illustrated cross-shaped symbol.
cards.back: The illustrated cross-shaped symbol warns of an intersection ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The upward arrow above a stop-sign symbol.
cards.back: The upward arrow above a stop-sign symbol warns that a stop sign is ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A space cushion is room around.
cards.back: A space cushion is room around the vehicle that provides more reaction time.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Maintain space on all sides.
cards.back: Maintain space on all sides according to speed and road conditions.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The basic following interval is at least four.
cards.back: The basic following interval is at least four seconds, with extra space needed in adverse conditions.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Measure a following gap from when the leading vehicle’s.
cards.back: Measure a following gap from when the leading vehicle’s rear passes a fixed point until your vehicle reaches it.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If you reach that point before four seconds have.
cards.back: If you reach that point before four seconds have elapsed, slow and recheck until the gap is at least four seconds.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Increase following distance on slippery roads and behind.
cards.back: Increase following distance on slippery roads and behind bicycles or motorcycles, especially where a rider may fall.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Ease speed slightly to help.
cards.back: Ease speed slightly to help a following driver complete a pass.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Leave more following space behind a large vehicle or.
cards.back: Leave more following space behind a large vehicle or trailer when its driver’s rear view or your forward view is restricted.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not pass a large vehicle on the right.
cards.back: Do not pass a large vehicle on the right when it may be preparing a wide right turn.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Consider large vehicles’ downhill momentum and uphill.
cards.back: Consider large vehicles’ downhill momentum and uphill speed loss when deciding whether to pass them.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When stopped behind a truck or bus.
cards.back: When stopped behind a truck or bus, leave rollback space, especially on a hill.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Increase the following gap at night, in fog or.
cards.back: Increase the following gap at night, in fog or bad weather, at high speed, with a heavy load or while towing.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Expect school buses and flammable-liquid tank trucks to stop.
cards.back: Expect school buses and flammable-liquid tank trucks to stop at railroad crossings and slow early to leave stopping room.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Avoid staying alongside another vehicle; pull ahead or fall.
cards.back: Avoid staying alongside another vehicle; pull ahead or fall back to preserve side space and avoid its blind spot.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Keep space from oncoming traffic.
cards.back: Keep space from oncoming traffic and avoid crowding the center line.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Give entering traffic room by.
cards.back: Give entering traffic room by changing lanes or slowing when feasible.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Avoid driving beside other vehicles near freeway exits because.
cards.back: Avoid driving beside other vehicles near freeway exits because they may suddenly exit or return to the freeway.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Leave side space beside parked cars and.
cards.back: Leave side space beside parked cars and extra room for pedestrians, children and cyclists.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When a tractor-trailer passes you, move toward the.
cards.back: When a tractor-trailer passes you, move toward the right side of your lane to increase separation.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Create extra following distance before slowing or turning, and.
cards.back: Create extra following distance before slowing or turning, and help rear traffic by keeping a steady speed and signaling early.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If a tailgater can pass in a lane.
cards.back: If a tailgater can pass in a lane to your right, move right to facilitate the pass.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Without a right lane, wait for a clear route.
cards.back: Without a right lane, wait for a clear route ahead and reduce speed gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass.

cards.front: Complete the rule: With parked cars on the right and oncoming cars.
cards.back: With parked cars on the right and oncoming cars on the left, choose a middle path that balances the hazards.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When a cyclist and an oncoming car would squeeze.
cards.back: When a cyclist and an oncoming car would squeeze the same gap, slow and let the car pass before overtaking the cyclist with three feet of room.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When merging, crossing or entering existing traffic, yield and.
cards.back: When merging, crossing or entering existing traffic, yield and allow enough room to avoid interfering with vehicles already there.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The manual calls for a four-second merging gap.
cards.back: The manual calls for a four-second merging gap for lane changes, freeway entry and road merges.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not squeeze into an undersized.
cards.back: Do not squeeze into an undersized gap; leave an adequate space cushion.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Cross multiple lanes one at a time rather than.
cards.back: Cross multiple lanes one at a time rather than stopping to wait for every lane to clear at once.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The from-stop crossing examples call for about half a.
cards.back: The from-stop crossing examples call for about half a city block or a full highway block of gap.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For turning into existing traffic, the examples allow about.
cards.back: For turning into existing traffic, the examples allow about two-thirds of a city block or two highway blocks to turn and accelerate.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Cross traffic only with room to finish; a halfway.
cards.back: Cross traffic only with room to finish; a halfway stop is safe only if a median is large enough to contain the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not enter an intersection, even on green.
cards.back: Do not enter an intersection, even on green, if vehicles or people block the onward path.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not rely solely on another driver’s turn signal.
cards.back: Do not rely solely on another driver’s turn signal; wait until the turn begins before acting on it.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Headlights improve the vehicle’s visibility to other road.
cards.back: Headlights improve the vehicle’s visibility to other road users during daylight as well as at night.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use headlights when visibility is too dim to see.
cards.back: Use headlights when visibility is too dim to see one thousand feet ahead or when the windshield wipers run continuously.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Maine requires headlights while.
cards.back: Maine requires headlights while driving from sunset through sunrise.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use headlights when driving away from a rising or.
cards.back: Use headlights when driving away from a rising or setting sun and whenever seeing other vehicles becomes difficult.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not substitute parking lights.
cards.back: Do not substitute parking lights alone when headlights are needed.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use high beams when possible, particularly on unfamiliar.
cards.back: Use high beams when possible, particularly on unfamiliar roads, in construction areas or near roadside people.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For a multiple-beam vehicle, dim or select low beam.
cards.back: For a multiple-beam vehicle, dim or select low beam within five hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle or when following within three hundred feet, and switch off an auxiliary fog light.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use low beams in fog, snow or.
cards.back: Use low beams in fog, snow or heavy rain to avoid reflected high-beam glare.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams.
cards.back: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, slow and look toward the right road edge; do not retaliate with your own bright beams.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use the horn for a needed collision-prevention warning.
cards.back: Use the horn for a needed collision-prevention warning, not without cause or merely to make loud noise.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A light early horn tap can warn a pedestrian.
cards.back: A light early horn tap can warn a pedestrian or cyclist entering the lane, a driver turning into your lane or someone who has not seen you.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Avoid startling cyclists or horses with the horn.
cards.back: Avoid startling cyclists or horses with the horn, but use a sharp warning when danger is near.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Signal before changing lanes, turning, merging, entering or leaving.
cards.back: Signal before changing lanes, turning, merging, entering or leaving a freeway or parking lot, or turning into a driveway.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Tap the brake to warn of a slowdown for.
cards.back: Tap the brake to warn of a slowdown for a turn without a separate exit lane or for parking or turning before an intersection.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Signal even if no other road user is visible.
cards.back: Signal even if no other road user is visible, and signal early enough to allow at least one hundred feet before a turn or change.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use hand signals when.
cards.back: Use hand signals when the electrical turn signals fail.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When the intended turn lies beyond an intersection.
cards.back: When the intended turn lies beyond an intersection, delay the signal until after passing that intersection.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After a turn or lane.
cards.back: After a turn or lane change, make sure the signal cancels.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A driver’s left arm held straight.
cards.back: A driver’s left arm held straight out horizontally signals a left turn.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A driver’s left arm bent.
cards.back: A driver’s left arm bent upward signals a right turn.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A driver’s left arm bent.
cards.back: A driver’s left arm bent downward signals slowing or stopping.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For a roadside breakdown, pull completely out of traffic.
cards.back: For a roadside breakdown, pull completely out of traffic if possible and use emergency flashers, or the appropriate turn signal if there are no flashers.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Raise the hood to indicate an emergency and stop.
cards.back: Raise the hood to indicate an emergency and stop where approaching drivers can see the vehicle, avoiding blind hilltops or curves.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If emergency flares are available, place them at.
cards.back: If emergency flares are available, place them at least one hundred feet behind the stopped car.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Without flares, remain off the roadway and use a.
cards.back: Without flares, remain off the roadway and use a cloth or flag if available to warn approaching traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not change a tire if it.
cards.back: Do not change a tire if it would require standing in a traffic lane.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Drive where others can see you and.
cards.back: Drive where others can see you and avoid remaining beside and slightly behind another vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Move ahead or fall back to leave another driver’s.
cards.back: Move ahead or fall back to leave another driver’s blind spot, and pass through it promptly when overtaking.
